cards.meaning: cannot be ignored / cannot be tolerated to be overlooked (a risk or problem serious enough that ignoring it has real consequences)
cards.example: 今天Ascend Analytics的报告说，到2030年，得州超过八成的大型用电项目可能拿不到匹配的发电量——这个风险不容忽视。
cards.examplePinyin: Jīntiān Ascend Analytics de bàogào shuō, dào 2030 nián, dézhōu chāoguò bāchéng de dàxíng yòngdiàn xiàngmù kěnéng ná bù dào pǐpèi de fādiànliàng — zhège fēngxiǎn bùróng hūshì.
cards.exampleMeaning: Today's Ascend Analytics report says that by 2030, more than 80% of Texas's large power-hungry projects may not have matching generation available — this risk cannot be ignored.
cards.note: 书面语/formal register — common in policy reports and analyst notes, typically paired with 问题/风险/趋势 (problem/risk/trend). Stronger than 值得关注 (worth paying attention to): 值得关注 just suggests noting something, while 不容忽视 is a warning that ignoring it carries real consequences.
cards.tiesTo: Energy segment — Ascend Analytics's warning that most large Texas loads chasing power won't have matching generation by 2030

cards.meaning: from this it can be seen that / this shows that (draws a conclusion from evidence just stated)
cards.example: 今天中国七月的工业增加值和零售数据同时不及预期，可以说：由此可见，出口和消费两方面同时放缓，问题不只是外部需求。
cards.examplePinyin: Jīntiān Zhōngguó qīyuè de gōngyè zēngjiāzhí hé língshòu shùjù tóngshí bùjí yùqī, kěyǐ shuō: yóucǐ kějiàn, chūkǒu hé xiāofèi liǎng fāngmiàn tóngshí fàng huǎn, wèntí bù zhǐ shì wàibù xūqiú.
cards.exampleMeaning: Today China's July industrial-production and retail figures both missed forecasts at once, so you could say: from this it can be seen that both exports and consumption are slowing at the same time — this isn't just an external-demand problem.
cards.note: 书面语/formal transition phrase, usually opens a sentence that summarizes preceding evidence — emphasizes the reasoning process. Casual speech uses simpler 看来 or 看样子 instead, which don't carry the same argumentative rigor as 由此可见.
cards.tiesTo: China segment — July industrial production and retail sales both missing forecasts at once

cards.meaning: corruption, malfeasance (abuse of entrusted authority, not just petty wrongdoing)
cards.example: Idinetalye ni dating DPWH Sekretaryo Bonoan ang umano'y katiwalian sa 24-bilyong-pisong "leadership fund."
cards.exampleMeaning: Former DPWH Secretary Bonoan detailed the alleged corruption in the 24-billion-peso "leadership fund."
cards.note: Stronger and more formal than the colloquial korap — korap reads as gossip or a casual accusation, while katiwalian is the term used in news reporting, investigative pieces, and formal proceedings like a Sandiganbayan case.
cards.tiesTo: Philippines — the ₱24 billion DPWH "leadership fund" testimony before the Sandiganbayan

cards.meaning: hesitation, uncertainty (doubt over whether to act, especially in a deliberative or institutional sense)
cards.example: Dahil sa mahinang GDP, nasa pag-aalinlangan ang BSP kung ipagpapatuloy pa nila ang mahigpit na patakaran sa interes.
cards.exampleMeaning: Because of the weak GDP print, the BSP is in a state of hesitation over whether to continue its tight interest-rate policy.
cards.note: Weightier and more institutional than the casual medyo nag-aalangan — the casual phrase sounds like everyday personal indecision, while pag-aalinlangan describes a more deliberate, consequential wavering, the kind a central bank weighs in public.
cards.tiesTo: Philippines — BSP Governor Remolona's cautious tone on further rate hikes after a weak Q2 GDP print
